title: Find the Number of Ways to Place People I
summary: Given a 2D array of points, count the number of unique pairs where one point is strictly to the left and above the other, with no other points in the line segment or rectangle formed by these points.
statement: Given a 2D array of points, count the number of unique pairs where one point is strictly to the left and above the other, with no other points in the line segment or rectangle formed by these points.
constraints: points contains at least two distinct integer coordinates.
Alice at A must satisfy A.x≤B.x and A.y≥B.y for Bob, allowing a zero-width or zero-height fence.
Count ordered role pairs whose closed rectangle contains no third point.
hints: After sorting x ascending and y descending, Bob candidates for one Alice are valid exactly when they set a new highest y not exceeding Alice.
Scan later points and count record-high y values bounded by Alice’s y.
Sort (x,-y); for each i keep max_y=-∞ and count y when max_y<y≤alice_y, then update max_y.
Any intervening y at least Bob’s lies inside the closed rectangle and blocks it; record highs are precisely the unblocked candidates.
editorial: Any intervening y at least Bob’s lies inside the closed rectangle and blocks it; record highs are precisely the unblocked candidates.

tests.explanation: Every left point is below each right point, so no Alice/Bob orientation is valid.
The two adjacent descending pairs are empty; the outer rectangle contains the middle point.
